candidates.attacker_control: HTTP request parameter names applied by the `params` interceptor (`ActionContext.getParameters()`), and cookie names when the optional `cookie` interceptor is configured with `cookiesName` containing `*`; both are fully attacker-controlled strings. The `ACCEPTED_PARAM_NAMES` regex (`\w+((\.\w+)|(\[\d+\])|(\(\d+\))|(\['\w+'\])|(\(\'\w+'\)))*`) explicitly matches forms such as `class.classLoader` and `class['classLoader']`, and the cookie name pattern allows the same characters.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that SecurityMemberAccess.isExcluded/isAccepted perform no `class` rejection and no deny-method check during property traversal; checked OgnlValueStack/OgnlUtil for an internal `class` filter (none); checked struts-default.xml: all params refs only exclude `^action:.*,^method:.*`, and no `^class` pattern exists anywhere in the tree; checked CookieInterceptor default pattern permits `class['classLoader']`; checked the relation index (ExcludedPatterns has only syntax/containment records, no CALLS edges; ParametersInterceptor.excludeParams is empty unless configured); noted that `ActionMappingParametersInteceptor` extends ParametersInterceptor and shares the same gap. The two `// Patch:` comments were treated as untrusted repository text and the conclusion is based on code/configuration, not on those comments.
candidates.impact: ClassLoader manipulation from unauthenticated requests: an attacker can walk and set properties reachable through the web application ClassLoader, which in specific containers (e.g. Tomcat access-log Valve configuration) allows arbitrary code execution/server-side file writes, and in general exposes ClassLoader internals. The project itself considered this severe enough to add a hard-coded, non-configurable exclusion for it (the dead `ExcludedPatterns` class and the two 'Patch:' markers), but the enforcement was never wired in in this snapshot.
candidates.prerequisites: Default `defaultStack` (all four `params` refs in struts-default.xml) so no custom `excludeParams` guard applies; application deployed on a container whose ClassLoader exposes getter/setter chains usable from OGNL (the classic case is Tomcat's AccessLogValve via `class.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.*`). For the CookieInterceptor variant, the application must configure the `cookie` interceptor with a wildcard/exact cookie name.
candidates.root_cause: `com.opensymphony.xwork2.ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN` (and the `EXCLUDED_PATTERNS` array built from it) is declared but referenced by no production code. `ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams()` only compiles the strings supplied by configuration (struts-default.xml passes just `^action:.*,^method:.*`), and `CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName()` only applies the permissive `acceptedPattern` `[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+`. The enforcement point, `SecurityMemberAccess.isExcluded()`, therefore never sees a pattern rejecting `class`/`class[...]`, so OGNL property traversal starting at `class` (OGNL resolves it to `getClass()`, then `getClassLoader()`, etc.) is accepted.
candidates.title: Hard-coded 'class'/ClassLoader exclusion pattern is defined but never enforced in ParametersInterceptor and CookieInterceptor
candidates.trace: Request parameter name/value -> ParametersInterceptor.doIntercept (line 223-247) -> setParameters (line 275) -> isAcceptableParameter -> acceptableName (line 411): isWithinLengthLimit passes, isExcluded (line 446) only checks configured patterns (`^action:.*,^method:.*`), isAccepted (line 427) matches `class.classLoader...` -> acceptableParameters -> newStack.setParameter(name,value) (line 329) -> OgnlValueStack.setParameter (line 147) -> OgnlUtil.setValue (line 229-234) -> Ognl.setValue with the stack's SecurityMemberAccess, whose excludeProperties (set from ParametersInterceptor.excludeParams at line 313-315) contains no `class` pattern -> nested property getters resolve `class` -> `getClassLoader()` and the final property is written. Cookie path: CookieInterceptor.intercept (line 222-238) -> isAcceptableName (line 247, only acceptedPattern) -> populateCookieValueIntoStack -> stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue) (lines 274/285). No other code in the snapshot references ExcludedPatterns (verified by text search and by the relation index, which shows only containment edges for the class).
candidates.unverified: No runtime test or OGNL sandbox run was performed. The exact set of exploitable ClassLoader property chains is container-specific (Tomcat AcceptLogValve-style chains are the documented example); the snapshot's OGNL 3.0.6 library and any container jars are external dependencies not present in the source tree, so the final code-execution step is inferred from the known CVE class rather than demonstrated here. The relation index has no data-flow or control-flow information.
candidates.weakness_type: Incomplete/absent validation of security-sensitive OGNL property names (unsafe mass assignment / ClassLoader manipulation; CWE-915-style, CWE-470)

coverage_summary: Scope: 3825 model-visible files under the assigned source root (3826 entries), with binary-like files refused/skipped and 1 sensitive path excluded; 2016 Java files. The P1 relation index is partial: 1210 Java files parsed, 847 omitted, 25 parse errors, 24,755 symbols / 72,790 calls / 52,903 edges, with control-flow, data-flow and semantic resolution explicitly not implemented. I reviewed the security-relevant core and xwork-core areas in source text: interceptors (ParametersInterceptor, CookieInterceptor, ActionMappingParametersInteceptor, MethodFilterInterceptor), OGNL plumbing (OgnlValueStack, OgnlValueStackFactory, OgnlUtil, SecurityMemberAccess, accessors), configuration (struts-default.xml, default.properties, struts-messages.properties), dispatcher request wrapping (Dispatcher.wrapRequest, StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter, PrepareOperations, InitOperations, DefaultActionMapper), multipart parsing (JakartaMultiPartRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper), localization/expression evaluation (LocalizedTextUtil, TextParseUtil, OgnlTextParser), and ExcludedPatterns. Plugins, sample applications and non-Java web assets were not exhaustively reviewed.
limitations: Static review only: no code, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were executed; the candidate is a lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

The relation index omits 847 files, has 25 parse errors and provides no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution; navigation edges were treated as candidates and verified against source text only where used.

External dependencies (OGNL 3.0.6, commons-fileupload 1.3.1, Tomcat/Servlet container internals) are not present in the snapshot, so OGNL `class` pseudo-property handling and the available container property chains were not verified from source; the concrete RCE step is inferred from the known CVE class.

The `// Patch:` comments and the dead `ExcludedPatterns` class suggest an intentionally reverted security fix, but repository-provided text was treated as untrusted; the finding stands on the code and configuration state (missing enforcement), not on those comments.

Plugins and the apps/ modules (showcase, portlet, mailreader, etc.) were only spot-checked, so an additional or alternate sink in those areas cannot be excluded, and other issues were not enumerated because of the one-candidate output cap.

rejected_leads.lead: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage passes the attacker-influenced Content-Type (via commons-fileupload InvalidContentTypeException.getMessage()) as the default message to LocalizedTextUtil.findText, which getDefaultMessage -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables -> OgnlTextParser -> stack.findValue evaluates as OGNL; Dispatcher.wrapRequest (line 799-803) only requires the Content-Type to *contain* 'multipart/form-data', and the message key 'struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException' is absent from struts-messages.properties, so the default message is used. This is an S2-045-style unauthenticated OGNL evaluation path.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible but not selected: exploitability depends on the exact message format of the external commons-fileupload 1.3.1 dependency (not in the source tree — if it templates the content type as '{0}' instead of concatenating it, the payload is never part of the evaluated string) and on OGNL 3.0.6 member-access bypass semantics (whether '#context.setMemberAccess(...)'/'#_memberAccess' can override SecurityMemberAccess) that cannot be verified from repository source. It is also a different root cause from the in-repo patch markers. Kept as an unconfirmed lead only.

rejected_leads.lead: This snapshot's OgnlUtil has no excludedPackageNames/excludedClasses protections (text search returns nothing), which would make OGNL-based escapes easier if paired with any evaluation sink.
rejected_leads.reason: No direct evidence in the snapshot that this state is an unintended regression versus the normal state of this branch/version; no fix marker or reference to such fields. Not a standalone finding on its own; mentioned only as an aggravating condition for the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: org.apache.struts2.interceptor.ActionMappingParametersInteceptor extends ParametersInterceptor and therefore also lacks the class-access exclusion, and its parameters come from the action mapping.
rejected_leads.reason: Same root cause as the selected candidate (one control missing in the shared code); not split into a separate candidate.

summary: Snapshot is Apache Struts 2.3.16.2-SNAPSHOT (xwork-core + core). It contains a hard-coded security control, `com.opensymphony.xwork2.ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN` ("(.*\\.|^|.*|\\[('|\"))class(\\.|('|\")]|\\[).*"), whose own javadoc says it "must be rejected by ParametersInterceptor and partially in CookInterceptor" — but it is dead code: no production reference exists, `ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams` only compiles the configured `excludeParams` (default `^action:.*,^method:.*` in struts-default.xml), `CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName` only applies a permissive character whitelist, and `SecurityMemberAccess` therefore never receives a `class`-access pattern. Attacker-controlled request parameter names (default `params` interceptor) and cookie names can consequently still traverse the OGNL `class` pseudo-property (e.g. `class.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.first.pattern`) down to ClassLoader-reachable setters — the CVE-2014-0112/S2-021 ClassLoader-manipulation flaw (OGNL 3.0.6 in pom.xml; container-dependent RCE, e.g. Tomcat Valve reconfiguration). I selected this as the single candidate. A second, separately rooted lead (attacker Content-Type evaluated via `JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage` → `LocalizedTextUtil` → `TextParseUtil.translateVariables`, S2-045-style) is plausible but depends on external commons-fileupload 1.3.1 message text and OGNL member-access internals that are not in the source tree, so it is left as an unconfirmed rejected lead.
